probe.question: For the amidation of CC(=O)O with NCc1ccccc1, I want one predictor's raw condition suggestions rather than the blended answer — take rxn_insight alone and show me what it proposes, so I can see how much of the consensus is coming from it.
forbids_claims: one predictor's condition set presented as the ensemble's consensus
a predicted yield for the suggested conditions
a claim about how much of the consensus this model contributed, computed from this call alone
probe.direction: The condition-side counterpart of pr-03 and the same judgement: this is interrogating a model, not answering a chemistry question. The answer must return that one predictor's ranked condition sets, in Celsius, and say so explicitly. The trap worth grading is the second half of the ask — "how much of the consensus is coming from it" cannot be answered by a single-model call, which returns no vote weights and no other model's output; answering it requires the ensemble call beside this one, and inventing a contribution share from one predictor's ranking is a fabrication. Saying what the call can and cannot settle, and offering the ensemble call as the way to settle the rest, is the right shape.
